newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up at close after slow session.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up at close after slow session.

text.p: Mexican stocks edged higher on Thursday in dull trading as U.S. financial markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday, and the Mexican Stock Exchange suspended open outcry to test an electronic trading system.
"Prices held steady, and gained a little towards the close on month-end buying. Nothing special happened, as you would expect in a consolidation period like this one," said a trader.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 4.25 points, or 0.13 percent, at 3,273.09.

In the broader market, 100 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 49 to 30. Only 50.1 million shares changed hands, and that figure was inflated by 17 million shares of cross trades in just two stocks.
"I liked the session, trading was interesting, even though the excitement and flavor of the outcry was lost," the broker said of the electronic trading system.
Autoparts maker Iasasa headed the gainers, up four centavos (1 cent) to 37 (5 cents), following a debt restructuring plan.

Publishing company Gfesa bounced back from a fall Wednesday to end second on the gainers' list, up 17 centavos (2 cents) at 1.83 pesos (13 cents), which some traders put down to expectations the firm would finalise a pending deal with Bankers Trust.
Food company Herdez headed the losers, down 10 centavos (1 cents) to 2.30 pesos (29 cents).

Dealers noted most trade was in stocks that do not list American Depositary Receipts in New York. Market heavyweight Telmex, normally top of the most-traded stocks list in Mexico, ended in a lowly and almost unheard-of sixth place Thursday.
Telmex slid six centavos (1 cent) to 11.90 pesos ($1.51).
